source_user: Advanced cluster case GDS-37: Evaluate GPUDirect Storage for checkpoint and dataset I/O in distributed training. Variant 37 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate storage throughput from GPU DMA, validate filesystem and kernel support, measure queue depth and tail latency, compare CPU-staged I/O, and test restart consistency after interruption. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Use an authorized, isolated test allocation with disposable data and an unchanged CPU-staged fallback; platform facts remain unknown until measured. Inventory GPU/storage/PCIe/NVMe and NUMA topology, filesystem and mount support, kernel, driver and runtime versions, permissions, container limits, affinities, file layout, request size, concurrency, queue depth, cache state, compression, and checkpoint durability. For variant 37, pre-register the falsifiable hypothesis that, after filesystem support and actual direct GDS activation are independently demonstrated, GDS reduces useful distributed-training checkpoint or dataset-I/O stall and/or host CPU versus a matched CPU-staged control at identical data, synchronization, caching, queueing, and persistence semantics, without a pre-set p99, error, integrity, or restart regression. Measure storage-device throughput separately from GPU-DMA throughput and end-to-end wall time: GB/s, checkpoint/read time, training stall, CPU%, GPU idle time, queue depth, p50/p95/p99 latency, retries, and per-rank skew, with synchronized timestamps, repeated cold/warm trials, units, and uncertainty. Verify path selection, checksums, metadata, all-rank completion, and recovery after an injected interruption. Roll back to CPU staging if prerequisites or activation are unproven, integrity/restart checks fail, tail/error thresholds are exceeded, or node-failure handling is unsafe; preserve logs and require expert review before any production claim.
risks: GDS may be unsupported or silently fall back to CPU staging.
Cache, compression, filesystem behavior, queueing, and shared-storage or node contention can confound causal comparisons.
Interrupted or node-failure checkpoints can appear successful without checksum and restart validation.
evidence_required: Read-only topology, filesystem/kernel support, permissions, and direct-path activation diagnostics
Matched CPU-staged and GDS logs with fixed workload and cache/queue/persistence conditions
Synchronized storage/DMA/end-to-end latency, throughput, CPU, and rank-skew measurements with units and uncertainty
Checksums, metadata/rank completeness, and successful interrupted-restart or node-failure recovery validation
